requirements.RCON-API-001: `createConnection(options)` returns an object whose one call is `run(name, { data, args, dataId })`.
requirements.RCON-API-002: `run` always resolves to a result object and never rejects, whatever is thrown underneath, including a bare string.
requirements.RCON-API-003: A call `run` cannot make sense of (no function name, data that is not an array of records, arguments that are not named) resolves to an `error` result whose message begins `bio.viz:`, and does not start R.
requirements.RCON-API-004: A connection is refused when it is created if a browser-form setting is malformed: packages that are not a list of valid R package names, a source that is not text, both a source and a source URL, a location that is not text, or an engine without `start` and `call`.
requirements.RCON-API-005: Both committed bundles export the connection and the formatter as `r.createConnection` and `r.formatStatistic`: `BioViz.r` on a page.
requirements.RCON-RES-001: When R answers, the result is `{ status: 'ok', value, form }`: the value R returned, and which form answered, `precomputed` or `browser`.
requirements.RCON-RES-002: With neither form configured, the result is `{ status: 'unavailable', reason: 'no-r-attached', message }`, and nothing is requested.
requirements.RCON-RES-003: When the R function fails, the result is `{ status: 'error', message }` with R's message.
requirements.RCON-PRE-001: With stored results, a call that has one is answered without starting R and without a network request.
requirements.RCON-PRE-002: A stored result is found by its function name, its arguments and its data identity together; the order the arguments are written in does not matter.
requirements.RCON-PRE-003: A call with no exact stored result is answered `unavailable` with reason `not-precomputed` and no value: another function, other arguments, other data, no data identity given, or a row count that differs from the one recorded.
requirements.RCON-PRE-004: Stored results that are malformed, or that hold two results under one key, are refused when the connection is created.
requirements.RCON-PRE-005: With both forms configured, a call with no stored result is answered by R in the browser.
requirements.RCON-PRE-006: Changing a value a call returned does not change the stored result.
requirements.RCON-LAZY-001: Creating a connection starts nothing; the first run that needs R starts the engine, with the location, packages and source the connection was given.
requirements.RCON-LAZY-002: Two simultaneous first calls cause one start, and later calls reuse it.
requirements.RCON-LAZY-003: A start that fails answers `unavailable` with reason `load-failed` and the cause, for every call waiting on it, and the next run tries again.
requirements.RCON-LAZY-004: In the browser form nothing is requested until the first run, and two simultaneous first runs load webR once.
requirements.RCON-ISO-001: Two connections share no state: each has its own stored results and starts its own engine.
requirements.RCON-WEBR-001: webR is pinned to version 0.6.0 and loaded from its public CDN unless another location is given; a location relative to the page is resolved against the page.
requirements.RCON-WEBR-002: webR is started on the PostMessage channel on every host.
requirements.RCON-WEBR-003: The R packages the connection was told to are installed and attached, and the R source it was given is evaluated once.
requirements.RCON-WEBR-004: An R source given by URL is fetched on the first run, not before, and once.
requirements.RCON-WEBR-005: A start that fails part-way closes the R session it opened and reports the cause.
requirements.RCON-CALL-001: The array of records goes to R as one column per variable, with the function name and the arguments, each as an R named list.
requirements.RCON-CALL-002: Every column has a value for every row; a value that is absent or not a number goes to R as missing.
requirements.RCON-CALL-003: The list R returns comes back as plain JavaScript objects, arrays, numbers, text and booleans.
requirements.RCON-CALL-004: Each kind of R value other than a data frame has one JavaScript shape: a named list or named vector is an object, an unnamed list is an array, an unnamed vector is a single value when its length is one and an array otherwise, and NULL or NA is null. A value with no plain form is an error.
requirements.RCON-CALL-005: An R error is reported with R's own message and nothing added, and the R objects made for a call are released whether it succeeds or fails.
requirements.RCON-CALL-006: Nested arguments go to R as nested lists, and a call with no data or no arguments sends none.
requirements.RCON-CALL-007: The R code that passes a table in and a result out uses base R only, and computes no statistic.
requirements.RCON-CALL-008: A data frame R returns, at any depth, comes back as an array of row objects, one per row, with every column in every row and NA as null: an empty array for no rows and an array of one object for one row, the same shape `data` has going in.
requirements.RCON-BUILD-001: The build bundles only files under `src/` and does not resolve the webR import.
requirements.RCON-BUILD-002: The committed bundles keep the import of webR as a run-time import of a URL and contain none of webR: every file a bundle names as one it was made from is a file under `src/`, and the bundles hold no known marker of webR's code.
requirements.RCON-BUILD-003: The `r` module imports nothing from outside `src/r/`, so the connection can be handed to a chart in another library.
requirements.RCON-CHECK-001: On the R check page two numbers count as the same answer when they differ by no more than 1 part in 10^8 of the larger; zero equals only zero, and something that is not a number equals nothing.
requirements.RCON-CHECK-002: Every member of an answer is compared with the expected one: numbers by the tolerance; text, counts, warnings and the shape of the answer exactly. A member missing or added fails.
requirements.RCON-CHECK-003: A number is shown in full, as the shortest text that reads back as exactly that number, so a difference in the last digit is visible.
requirements.RCON-CHECK-004: The page's tables are read from CSV with their numeric columns as numbers and blanks as missing.
requirements.RCON-CHECK-005: The committed expected results name the script, the R version and the survival version that made them.
requirements.RCON-CHECK-006: Each expected result is a stored result on its committed table: given to the precomputed form with that table, it is answered.
requirements.RCON-PAGE-001: The R check page has a button that starts R and does not start it otherwise; it states the tolerance and the R and survival versions that made the desktop answers.
requirements.RCON-PAGE-002: The page shows the recorded megabytes, requests, requests answered from the network and seconds for three states named separately, cold, reload and warm, with the browser, machine, date and method of the measurement.
requirements.RCON-PAGE-003: With no measurement recorded the page says so and prints no number in its place.
requirements.RCON-LIVE-001: On the R check page, with no R attached, the call answers that statistics are unavailable.
requirements.RCON-LIVE-002: On the R check page the precomputed form gives the desktop-R answers for both tests with no R loaded and no request to R's hosts.
requirements.RCON-LIVE-003: R started in the browser gives the Wilcoxon rank-sum result desktop R gives, within the stated tolerance.
requirements.RCON-LIVE-004: The survival package installs and loads in the browser, and the log-rank result is the one desktop R gives, within the stated tolerance.
requirements.RCON-LIVE-005: Cold, a first visit with nothing cached: megabytes over the network, requests and seconds to the first result are measured, and webR is loaded once from the pinned version on its public CDN.
requirements.RCON-LIVE-006: Reload, the page loaded again with the files in the browser's cache: R starts again, gives the same answers, and less comes over the network than on the first visit; megabytes, requests and seconds are measured.
requirements.RCON-LIVE-007: Warm, R already running in the page: a repeated call makes no request and takes less time than the first result; its seconds are measured.
requirements.RCON-LIVE-008: The R check page holds at a 390-pixel-wide viewport with no horizontal scroll, with its results shown.
requirements.RCON-LIVE-009: The three measurements are printed in the run's log, attached to the test and written to a file, with the browser, the machine and how sizes were counted.
requirements.PVAL-FMT-001: An ordinary p-value is printed to three decimals, after the method's name and before the counts used.
requirements.PVAL-FMT-002: A p-value below 0.001 is printed as `p < 0.001`, never as zero or in exponent form.
requirements.PVAL-FMT-003: A p-value that would round to 1.000 is printed as `p > 0.999`.
requirements.PVAL-FMT-004: Counts are printed for each group by name, or as one total.
requirements.PVAL-RULE-001: A p-value whose result names no method is refused: the text says so and prints no number.
requirements.PVAL-RULE-002: A p-value whose result gives no counts is refused: the text says so and prints no number.
requirements.PVAL-RULE-003: A result is labelled exploratory, and unadjusted unless the result names an adjustment, which is then named.
requirements.PVAL-RULE-004: The text never contains a star or the word significant, however small the p-value.
requirements.PVAL-RULE-005: Where R gave a reason in place of a number, such as a group too small to test, the reason is printed and no number is.
requirements.PVAL-RULE-006: A p-value that is not a number from 0 to 1 is refused, not repaired.
requirements.PVAL-RULE-007: The formatter computes nothing: the same result always gives the same text, and the result is left unchanged.
requirements.PVAL-RULE-008: A reason that already says the result was not computed is printed as it is, with the counts after it, so that "not computed" is said once.
requirements.PVAL-RULE-009: A result R marked as an error is printed as R's message, said to be an error, with the counts where R knew them and no number.
requirements.PVAL-RULE-010: An adjustment R names by its `p.adjust` method is printed by its usual name, `holm` as Holm and `BH` as Benjamini-Hochberg; any other name is printed as given.
requirements.PVAL-EST-001: An estimate is printed with its name, what it is an estimate of, and its interval with the level R gave, each number to four significant figures; an estimate with no interval is printed without one.
requirements.PVAL-EST-002: An estimate with no name or no finite number, or with an interval that has a part missing, is refused, and no number is printed in its place.
requirements.PVAL-ROW-001: One comparison of two groups from a result's rows is formatted by the rules a whole result is held to: its p-value, the adjusted one, comes with its method, the two groups' counts and its label, and is handed over in parts for a table only with them.
requirements.PVAL-ROW-002: A comparison with no method, no counts or no two groups is refused, and one R could not compute shows R's words and no number.
requirements.PVAL-GRP-001: One group's result from a result's rows is formatted by the rules a whole result is held to: its estimate comes with its interval at the level R gave, or with none where R gave none, and its p-value with its method, the group's count and its label; all are handed over in parts for a table only together.
requirements.PVAL-GRP-002: A group's result with no group name, no method, no count, no estimate or half an interval is refused, and one R could not compute shows R's words and no number.
